name: Centro Historico
description: Campeche's UNESCO-listed core sits within old defensive walls, a grid of brightly painted streets, plazas, bastions and terraces. It is the most walkable, atmospheric and tourist-friendly part of the city, packed with cafes, restaurants and colonial charm at every turn.
bestFor: Nomads wanting atmosphere, walkability and cafes within the colonial walled centre
pros: Best choice of cafes and restaurants
cons: Can feel touristy in peak season

name: Malecon Waterfront
description: Running along the Gulf of Mexico, the malecon is Campeche's long seafront promenade, popular for walking, running and evening strolls. Nearby modern flats and hotels offer sea breezes and open views, a short walk from the historic centre.
bestFor: Those wanting sea views, breezes and space for waterfront walks and runs
cons: Fewer cafes right on the front

name: San Roman and Guadalupe
tagline: Traditional barrios just outside the walls
description: These historic neighbourhoods sit just beyond the walled centre, built around old churches and squares. They keep an authentic, local feel with cheaper rents, neighbourhood eateries and everyday Campeche life, while remaining an easy walk from the historic core.
bestFor: Budget-minded nomads wanting authentic local life near the historic centre

name: Avenida Central and San Francisco
description: North and inland toward Avenida Central and the San Francisco district lies Campeche's more modern, practical side, with supermarkets, services, malls and newer housing. It trades colonial charm for convenience and value, suiting longer stays that prioritise everyday amenities.
bestFor: Longer-stay nomads prioritising amenities, supermarkets and lower everyday costs
